key_idea: Minimise max(n_i + D*depth_i) over binary trees: Huffman-style, repeatedly merge the two smallest arrival times into max(a,b)+D.
sketch: Put all n_i in a min-heap; pop the two smallest a,b and push max(a,b)+D until one value remains, then add L. The exchange argument is the same as for Huffman coding with the max+c cost: the two earliest signals can always be siblings at the deepest level. O(N log N) with N=4e5. Values reach about 1e9 + 4e5*1e9 in the degenerate chain, so use 64-bit. An alternative is binary search on T with a Kraft-inequality check.
